title: Emergency Medicine Scheduling Software | Done For You
description: Emergency medicine scheduling software can be a burden on chief residents. Scheduling Wizard is a managed service that builds the schedule for you, to your rules and the ACGME requirements.
h1: Emergency Medicine Scheduling, Built For You
paragraph: As a chief resident, just submit your EM program's rules, and Scheduling Wizard delivers your finished schedule.

cta.title: Get Your EM Schedules Done Right
cta.description: Book a call to talk through your scheduling needs and learn how Scheduling Wizard works. Join 30+ departments across 20+ hospitals and practices that have us build their call, block, clinic and shift schedules.

faq.answer: It is built to the ACGME requirements you tell us apply, alongside your own rules, and we check the finished schedule against them before it goes out. The review on your side is a check, not a repair job. The EM requirements you tell us apply are built in, including duty hour limits and rest requirements. It is the first thing most programs ask, and the answer is the same: you tell us which requirements apply, we write them down with you, and we build to them.
faq.question: Is Scheduling Wizard compliant with ACGME rules for emergency medicine?

faq.answer: Most emergency medicine scheduling software is self-service, meaning a chief resident must learn the platform, enter all the rules, and troubleshoot conflicts themselves. Scheduling Wizard is a managed service. Programs submit their rules and receive finished schedules, built to your rules, as Excel or Google Sheets, or on a custom live view we build for you. There is no software to learn and no platform to operate.
faq.question: How is Scheduling Wizard different from other emergency medicine scheduling software?

faq.answer: Scheduling Wizard generates block and rotation schedules, call schedules, clinic schedules, and attending schedules for emergency medicine programs. All schedule types are built together, so that a change in one does not create conflicts in another. Finished schedules are delivered as Excel or Google Sheets, or on a custom live view we build for you.
faq.question: What types of EM schedules does Scheduling Wizard generate?

faq.answer: Yes. Many Scheduling Wizard clients use the platform they already have for day-to-day schedule viewing. Scheduling Wizard handles the schedule building, and the finished schedule goes into whatever platform you already use. The two tools serve different functions and work well alongside each other.
faq.question: Can Scheduling Wizard integrate with your existing platform?

faq.answer: When an unexpected absence occurs, Scheduling Wizard rebuilds the affected portion of the schedule to restore coverage; turnaround depends on how much the change touches. This avoids the manual process of reshuffling assignments and checking every downstream impact by hand. The same rules are applied in the rebuild.
faq.question: What happens when an EM resident has an unplanned absence?

faq.answer: Chief resident transitions are one of the most common sources of scheduling disruption in EM programs. With Scheduling Wizard, your program's rules stay written down with us year over year. Incoming chief residents inherit the written rule set and last year's schedule instead of starting from scratch with a blank spreadsheet.
faq.question: How does Scheduling Wizard handle the annual chief resident transition?

I'm interested in a scheduling software that can integrate with the tools you already use and remove the administrative burden on our chief residents by providing schedules built to the ACGME requirements ready for use.
